title: Link Each Node to Its Right Neighbour
statement:
You get a perfect binary tree: every level is completely full, so every node has either two children or none, and all leaves are on the same depth. Give every node an extra pointer next that points to the node directly to its right on the same level. The rightmost node of each level gets next = null.

Try to use only O(1) extra memory besides the next pointers themselves (the recursion stack does not count).

The harness cannot inspect next pointers directly, so after linking, return what they produce: for each level from top to bottom, start at the leftmost node and follow next until null, collecting the values. Return the list of those rows. An empty tree gives []. Set next as a new property on the nodes ((node as any).next in TypeScript, node.next in Python).

examples.why: 5 links to 6 even though they have different parents. That cross-parent link is the part people miss.
A single node has no neighbour, so its next is null.

constraints: 0 ≤ number of nodes ≤ 4095 (a perfect tree, so 2^d − 1 nodes)
hints: Level-order traversal visits each level left to right. Linking neighbours from a queue is straightforward. Can you avoid the queue?
Once a level is linked, you can walk across it using next pointers alone, like a linked list.
While walking level L via next, link level L + 1: node.left.next = node.right, and node.right.next = node.next.left when node.next exists. Then drop down to the leftmost child and repeat.

explain.intuition:
With a queue, this is plain level-order traversal: pop the nodes of one level in order and link each to the one after it. That costs O(width) memory for the queue.

The O(1) trick is that the links you build become the queue. Suppose level L is already linked. Walk it left to right through next. Each node links its own two children (left.next = right), and its right child to the left child of the next node over (right.next = node.next.left). That second link is the cross-parent one. When the walk ends, level L + 1 is fully linked and you start again from its leftmost node. Because the tree is perfect, every node on a non-leaf level has both children, so there are no gaps to skip.
steps: If the tree is empty, return []. Set leftmost = root.
For each cur: set cur.left.next = cur.right; if cur.next exists, set cur.right.next = cur.next.left.
To build the output, start each row at the leftmost node of a level and follow next.
pitfalls: Linking only siblings that share a parent. In example 1 the link 5 → 6 crosses parents.
Linking the last node of a level to the first node of the next level. The rightmost node's next must stay null.

solutions.title: Level order with a queue
solutions.idea: Process one level at a time and link each node to the one after it in the queue.

solutions.title: Walk each level through its own links
solutions.idea: A linked level acts as a linked list. Walk it to link the level below, including the cross-parent links.

followups: The tree is no longer perfect: nodes may miss children. How do you find the next child to link to on the level below?
Use the next pointers to print the tree level by level without any queue.
